Definition: A set of colors and shapes used by all of the controls in a program so they look like they belong together.
A theme with dark text on light backgrounds.
A theme with light text on dark backgrounds.
The Quorum object that holds a program's theme. Every control asks it for its colors.
A smaller set of interface options stored under a name, such as "Button" or "Calendar". Controls that use that name get those colors first.
A color set on one control. It replaces the theme's color for that control only.
How different two colors look from each other. Text needs high contrast with its background to be easy to read.
